You are judging whether a task-assignment scenario satisfies three frozen scheduling requirements.

Requirements (authoritative; evaluate ALL of them against the scenario facts):
R1: Dependencies form a directed acyclic graph and every predecessor finishes before its successor starts.
R2: Two tasks writing the same resource may not execute at overlapping times; different-resource writers may overlap.
R3: Every task must have a finite start and end time with start strictly less than end.

Scenario facts:
Tasks (start/end are integers; end is exclusive): {"A":{"start":1,"end":4,"resource":"r"},"B":{"start":3,"end":5,"resource":"r"},"C":{"start":0,"end":2,"resource":"q"}}
Precedence edges (["A","B"] means A must finish before B starts): []

Tool evidence — faithful QF_LIA encoding of the fixed scenario facts (pinned receipt input_sha256 ca631d9eadaccc8f4f1cf372ca39a977c707974f78138244b7fe2f52dd854614):
(set-logic QF_LIA)
(declare-const start_A Int)
(declare-const end_A Int)
(assert (= start_A 1))
(assert (= end_A 4))
(declare-const start_B Int)
(declare-const end_B Int)
(assert (= start_B 3))
(assert (= end_B 5))
(declare-const start_C Int)
(declare-const end_C Int)
(assert (= start_C 0))
(assert (= end_C 2))
(assert (< start_A end_A))
(assert (< start_B end_B))
(assert (< start_C end_C))
(declare-const rank_A Int)
(declare-const rank_B Int)
(declare-const rank_C Int)
(assert (or (<= end_A start_B) (<= end_B start_A)))
(check-sat)

An independent SMT solver (Z3 5.4.0, exit code 0) evaluated this faithful QF_LIA encoding of R1-R3 over the fixed scenario facts. SAT means all encoded requirements are consistent with the facts; UNSAT means at least one encoded requirement is violated by the facts. Observed result: UNSAT.

Reason step by step, then end your reply with exactly one final line, no backticks:
VERDICT: PASS
or
VERDICT: FAIL
or
VERDICT: UNKNOWN
PASS = the scenario satisfies ALL of R1, R2, R3. FAIL = at least one requirement is violated. UNKNOWN = you cannot determine.
